-------------

Global-e Integration — Kick-off & Requirements Alignment

Date and Time
-------------

15 July 2026 — 11:00 AM

Attendees
---------

| Name | Role / Affiliation |
| --- | --- |
| Timothy Boyd | Global-e |
| Luke Holtfreter | Global-e |
| Volodymyr Dendevych | Global-e |
| Sean Doonan | Global-e |
| Lucy Fu | Zimmermann |
| Rebecca Jourdan | Zimmermann |
| Emma Kirwan | Zimmermann |
| Natasha Lay | Accenture |
| Charmaine Lew | Accenture |
| Manikandan Ramachandran | Accenture |
| Hardi Sempuno | Accenture |
| Navarro, Marcel Angelo N. | Accenture |
| victor.t.crisostomo | Accenture |

---

Agenda Items
------------

### 1. Overview & Architecture Confirmation

* Charmaine opened by demoing the new Zimmermann website.
* Timothy confirmed Global-e's approach: design is fully controlled by Zimmermann across all pages **except** the Global-e checkout, which is an iframe.
* Manikandan confirmed the storefront is **fully headless** — no SFRA, PWA Kit only.
* The checkout flow is triggered via a **Send Cart hook** that passes basket contents to Global-e. The Global-e checkout renders as a **1-page iframe checkout**, which aligns with current designs.
* Global-e handles: duties & taxes calculation, local payment methods, and the order confirmation screen within the iframe.
* SFCC still creates the order after Global-e checkout completes (OOTB Global-e cartridge behaviour) — order is then forwarded to NewStore.

### 2. Pricing Strategy

* Two pricing strategies are supported per market (one strategy per country, determined by Zimmermann):
* **Dynamic pricing** — calculated from a base price; Global-e manages the conversion and applies coefficients. Not real-time but fast. Global-e stores in their database and sends back to SFCC.
* **Fixed pricing** — fixed pricebook created and maintained in SFCC by Zimmermann. Global-e does **not** need these synced back; they are managed entirely in SFCC.
* Current implementation is a mix of both dynamic and fixed, market dependent.
* Timothy confirmed Global-e needs the **full list of countries/storefronts** and **base currencies per site** from Zimmermann.
* Luke flagged this should not be assumed as a straight lift-and-shift — Zimmermann should confirm whether they want to continue with the same mapping or make adjustments.
* Natasha raised the importance of understanding existing **Magento limitations** so the team can identify what can be improved in the SFCC implementation.

### 3. Order Flow & Fraud Check

* Global-e performs a **fraud check** before forwarding the confirmed order back to SFCC.
* **Do not forward to NewStore** until fraud check is passed and order status is updated by Global-e.
* If the order is fraudulent, Global-e cancels it and SFCC is notified.
* Global-e sends all **transactional emails** (order confirmation, etc.) — these are not sent until after the fraud check passes.
* Timothy to share: full order status list and email trigger sequence.

input.content:
# Learning Walkthrough — Compiling "Outstanding Items" & Auditing Docs Across Systems

> **Audience:** FED lead / anyone who has to turn "what are we waiting on?" into a clean,
> trustworthy answer — and keep the project's shared docs (Confluence/Jira) honest.
> **Based on:** the real *Zimmermann Outstanding Items* work — Natasha's ask ("outline the key
> outstanding actions we're waiting on Zimmermann for"), the parallel update to the Confluence
> **8.1 Technical Files (Zimm Provided)** page, and the Sparro / MuleSoft provenance chase.
> **Format:** what we did → the project map → transferable method → gotchas (incl. real mistakes) →
> reusable runbooks → key references → self-check.
> **Status of this doc:** personal learning artifact — not part of any PR.

---

## 1. TL;DR — what we actually did

Three intertwined pieces of work:

1. **Compiled a client-facing list** of key outstanding actions/questions we're waiting on
   Zimmermann for → `~/Documents/zimmermann-key-actions-awaiting.md`. It went through *two*
   versions: v1 was an accurate-but-broad register (everything from `openItems.md`); v2 was the
   re-cut that actually answered the question asked.
2. **Updated the Confluence "Zimm Provided" page** (8.1, id `264765445`) to record the Sparro
   JSON-LD templates and the MuleSoft docs — then hit trouble, reverted, and the human finished it
   by hand (attaching the real PDFs + a Google-Sheet link).
3. **Traced provenance** of the Sparro template and verified the MuleSoft PDFs against the
   codebase citations.

The most valuable output wasn't any single file — it was the **method** for doing this kind of
cross-system, client-facing work without over-claiming or breaking shared docs.

---

## 2. The project map I now carry in my head

Zimmermann's "what are we waiting on / what was provided" information is **scattered across
purpose-built homes**. Knowing which is which saves hours and prevents duplicate pages.

| Artifact | Where | What it's for |
|---|---|---|
| `openItems.md` | repo `.docs/temp/` | Accenture's consolidated integration open-items register (41 items / 18 integrations). The raw source of truth for "what's outstanding." |
| `.docs/vendor/*.md` | repo | **Downstream copies** of vendor docs (Sparro, MuleSoft, GiveX, Global-e, Didomi, Optimizely, Measmerize) — a *signal*, not a source (see provenance below). |
| **8.1 Technical Files (Zimm Provided)** | Confluence `264765445` | Catalogue of docs Zimmermann/vendors handed over. |
| **7.1b Third Party Credentials** | Confluence `268337165` | The per-vendor credential/ID tracker — columns: System · Credentials · Environments · **Who Provides** · Status. This is where the "waiting on Zimmermann for keys" story lives. |
| **`<Vendor>` — Open Questions for SFCC/PWA Design** | Confluence (MuleSoft `320602113`, Global-e `330235905`) | Per-integration technical open questions *with vendor responses filled in*. The live technical Q&A. |
| **Meeting notes** | Confluence under **8.2** (e.g. Data Dictionary `346587138`, Global-e `331218950`) | Decisions + action items with owners/dates. |
| **Jira SFCC-*** | Jira | The work itself — epics/stories that consume these dependencies (e.g. SFCC-22 analytics, SFCC-101 Measmerize, SFCC-188 PDP video). |

**Ownership model — the single most useful lens.** Every "outstanding item" is really one of:
- **A decision only Zimmermann can make** (consent approach, MFA scope, content ownership).
- **Access/credentials only Zimmermann can provide** (merchant IDs, API keys, Notice IDs).
- **A vendor deliverable Zimmermann must chase** — Zimmermann owns the vendor relationship, so
  it's *their* action to unblock even though the deliverable is the vendor's.
- **Our (Accenture) homework** — not waiting on anyone else (e.g. the data-layer *spec* we owe
  Tell No Lies; the `sfPayments` hostname design call).

Named owners worth remembering (from 7.1b + meetings): **Gus** (Omneo), **Simon** (MuleSoft),
**Billy** (GiveX), **Powerfront** (Inside Chat), **Vicky** (Zimmermann) + **Andrew** (TNL) for the
data dictionary, **Tim** (ACN architect).

**Hard blockers as of this work:** Omneo Communication-Preferences iFrame (×3 — no identifiers,
embed URL, or HMAC secret yet), and the credential sets for Contentful / Adyen / Global-e /
Google Places. The Tell No Lies **data dictionary** is the analytics critical-path input.

---

## 3. The transferable method (the real lesson)

### 3.1 Provenance, not proximity
A doc sitting in `.docs/vendor/` is a **downstream copy**, not its origin. `sparroSchema.md`'s own
header even says "*Source: Sparro Schema Templates 1025.xlsx (received 4 Jun 2026 from Sparro)*."
When the task is "record what Zimmermann provided," you must cite the **original delivery**
(the file, from whom, via what channel), not the repo path. If you can't confirm the channel,
say so and mark it a **placeholder** — never invent a source, never fall back to the repo path.
> *Reality check:* I had no email/Teams/SharePoint access, so several provenances were
> "partially confirmed" (file name + date + org known; channel unknown). Being explicit about that
> gap is the correct move, not glossing it.

### 3.2 Discovery → propose → approval-gate → execute
For anything touching shared systems or a client deliverable: **investigate read-only first,
report findings + a plan, get explicit approval, then act.** One clarifying decision at a time
beats a batch. This is slower but it's why the mistakes below were contained rather than shipped.

### 3.3 Scope the deliverable to the *actual* question
The v1→v2 lesson. v1 was **factually correct and useless-for-the-ask**: titled "Zimmermann *&
Vendors*," 42 exhaustive items, framed as open-items. Natasha asked for **"key actions we're
waiting on *Zimmermann*"**. Three axes were off:
- **Ownership** — half the items were vendor- or Accenture-owned, not Zimmermann's.
- **"Key"** — 42 items is a register, not a shortlist.
- **Framing** — open-items, not direct asks ("Zimmermann to confirm/provide/chase…").

> **Takeaway:** *accuracy ≠ alignment.* Always re-read the literal ask and test your draft against
> its exact words (who / how-many / what-form) before sending.

### 3.4 Verify across systems before asserting — and remember snapshots go stale
`openItems.md` was a point-in-time snapshot (last touched 2026-07-16). Cross-checking against
Confluence/Jira caught that: the MuleSoft **prod host** was since confirmed (`mw.zimmermann.com`),
the **GiveX** balance-check spec was already shared, the **Global-e** section predated the 15-Jul
meeting, and **GTM container IDs** were missing. A parallel subagent audited the codebase leg while
I did the Confluence/Jira legs — and the three legs together *cleared* items any single leg
couldn't verify (e.g. SFCC-173/174 exist in Jira even though they're absent from the repo).

---

## 4. Gotchas & real mistakes (the expensive lessons)

### 4.1 Editing a shared Confluence page by full-content replacement is dangerous
The Confluence update API replaces the **whole page body**. To change two cells I had to reproduce
~16 KB of storage-format XHTML — and I introduced two errors: a stray space in a `local-id`, and
(worse) I **silently dropped the entire Measmerize row** in a later edit. Lessons:
- **Prefer the human editing in the Confluence UI** for anything non-trivial on a live shared page.
- If you must edit programmatically, **fetch fresh storage immediately before**, change the
  minimum, and **verify with a version diff (`from_version`→`to_version`) afterward** — the diff
  is what caught the dropped row.
- **Markdown view hides file-embed macros** — a cell can look "empty" in markdown yet contain
  attachments. Check the *storage* format to be sure.

### 4.2 Shared docs move under you
Between my edit (v15) and my next read, the page jumped to **v16** — someone/something re-saved it

# What I Learned: Sorting "What We're Waiting on Zimmermann For"

*Plain-English notes for me (FED Lead). Simplified, not dumbed down — I want to actually reuse this, not wade through jargon.*
*From the Zimmermann "Outstanding Items" work.*

---

## In one line
Natasha asked for "the key actions/questions we're waiting on Zimmermann for." I pulled the list together, tidied up a couple of Confluence pages, and — along the way — figured out how the project's info is organised and how to do this kind of thing without tripping over myself.

---

## The mental model that makes all of this click: **"Whose job is it?"**

Every "outstanding thing" drops into one of four buckets. Asking this one question sorts almost all of the mess:

1. **Zimmermann has to decide it** — e.g. *"do we hide this script behind cookie consent, or let it run?"*
2. **Zimmermann has to hand it over** — logins, keys, IDs. We literally can't make these ourselves.
3. **A vendor delivers it, but Zimmermann has to chase them** — Zimmermann owns the relationship with Omneo, MuleSoft, Global-e, etc. So even though the thing comes *from the vendor*, getting it moving is still *Zimmermann's* job.
4. **It's actually our job** — nothing to wait on; we just haven't done it yet.

Think of a shared chore list. If someone asks *"what am I on the hook for?"*, you don't hand them the whole list — you hand them **their** chores. Buckets 1–3 are Zimmermann's chores. Bucket 4 is ours and shouldn't be on their list at all.

*(This is the thing I got wrong the first time — see Lesson 2.)*

---

## Where the project actually keeps this info (so I stop hunting for it)

It's spread across a few homes, each with a job. Knowing which is which stops me from creating a duplicate page:

- **`openItems.md`** *(our repo)* — the master list of everything outstanding across the ~18 integrations. **Start here.**
- **"8.1 Technical Files (Zimm Provided)"** *(Confluence)* — the shelf where docs Zimmermann/vendors gave us are catalogued.
- **"7.1b Third Party Credentials"** *(Confluence)* — the checklist of logins/keys we're waiting for, and **who provides each**.
- **"<Vendor> — Open Questions"** pages *(Confluence — e.g. MuleSoft, Global-e)* — the running Q&A with each vendor, **with their answers filled in**. This is the *live* status.
- **Meeting notes** *(Confluence)* — decisions + who owns the follow-up.
- **Jira (the SFCC-### tickets)** — the actual build work that depends on all of the above.

**Rule of thumb:** credentials → *7.1b* · provided docs → *8.1* · live vendor answers → the *Open-Questions* page · decisions → *meeting notes*.

---

## The 5 lessons worth keeping

**1. A copy isn't the original.**
We keep copies of vendor docs in the repo. But if someone asks *"where did this come from?"*, the repo copy isn't the answer — it's a photocopy. The real answer is *who sent it, when, and how*. If I can't confirm that, I say "source not confirmed" and flag it — I don't guess, and I don't point at the repo folder as if that were the source.

**2. Right facts, wrong question.**
My first draft of the list was 100% accurate — and still *wrong*, because it answered a bigger question than the one asked. **5. Klarna — contradiction to reconcile.** Doc says "Zimmermann-managed / out of Accenture scope."
